external_tools.name: n8n
external_tools.whatItDoes: Workflow automation platform. scripts/n8n/build-factory-workflow.ts and build-workflow-json.ts generate real, importable n8n workflow JSON (n8n/factory-v1.json, n8n/businessforge-workflow.json) targeting a real n8n instance's actual API/CLI (docker exec n8n import:workflow, the REST activate endpoint, the webhook trigger URL). n8n/README.md documents a concrete, n8n-specific engineering constraint that shaped the design: n8n 2.x's NodesConfig excludes n8n-nodes-base.executeCommand by default, so the workflow uses first-class HTTP Request nodes against scripts/n8n/stage-server.ts (0.0.0.0:7717, token-authenticated) instead of running commands inside n8n itself; the README also documents troubleshooting node typeVersion mismatches by inspecting the installed n8n-nodes-base package inside a running `docker exec n8n ...` container.
external_tools.currentImplementation: REAL_IMPLEMENTED (code level) — the generators, the stage-server HTTP API, and n8n/README.md's operational runbook (Docker container name, node typeVersion pinning verified against an actually-installed n8n instance, curl commands for activation and the live webhook) are strong, specific evidence this was built against and exercised on a real n8n deployment, not invented from n8n's public docs alone. Whether an n8n instance is *currently* running in this project's production environment right now is a deployment fact this repo pass cannot verify (no live network access to any n8n host) — recorded as UNKNOWN at that layer only, distinct from the code-level finding.
external_tools.rationale: 'n8n' is not a legacy naming convention — scripts/n8n/*.ts genuinely targets a real n8n instance, and the design (HTTP-only, no Execute Command nodes) is a direct, documented response to a real n8n 2.x security default. scripts/n8n/stage-server.ts remains the confirmed production entrypoint. WQ-015 resolved 2026-08-25: see n8n/README.md, scripts/n8n/build-workflow-json.ts, scripts/n8n/build-factory-workflow.ts.

duplications_found.summary: lib/capability/plan.ts's planCapability (cost-aware) and lib/ai/router.ts's routeCapability (availability/latency-only) are two independent capability-routing implementations, split along the Forge-vs-classic pipeline boundary.
duplications_found.resolution: ADR 0008 already resolves the ARCHITECTURAL fork this duplication sits on: classic pipeline is canonical, Forge REASONING modules are adopted into it. This registry recommends the ROUTER duplication itself (not yet explicitly addressed by an ADR) follow the same logic: lib/ai/router.ts stays canonical for the classic pipeline's stage-level provider selection; lib/capability/plan.ts's richer cost-aware planCapability/orchestrator should be treated as the model for any FUTURE unification, given it strictly dominates routeCapability on the ranking dimensions.
duplications_found.action: DOCUMENT, do not merge without a dedicated task — merging live routers is exactly the kind of unjustified architecture change the MASTER RULE prohibits without justification beyond this registry entry.

gaps.detail: lib/workflow/state.ts was purpose-built to unify main.ts's STAGES, jobState.ts's JobStage, and stage.ts's own STAGES array; it now has one real production importer (lib/workflow/summary.ts, via stageMapping.ts) but the three concrete vocabularies themselves are still what CLI/job.json/n8n actually run on.
gaps.recommendedNextStep: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (docs/WORK_QUEUE.json WQ-006 audit, WQ-019 step 1/2): WQ-006 found state.ts is NOT a strict superset of jobState.ts's 17 or stage.ts's 23 stage names. WQ-019 then did the real semantic mapping design WQ-006 called for: lib/workflow/stageMapping.ts documents, for every one of jobState.ts's 17 JobStage values, which state.ts abstract state it folds into -- derived by reading every saveJob(outputDir, {stage: ...}) call in scripts/n8n/stage.ts directly, not inferred from names. Exports JOB_STAGE_TO_ABSTRACT (compile-time-exhaustive) and abstractStageOf() (the back-compat reader -- degrades to null for an unrecognised stage string rather than throwing). Wired additively into summary.ts as JobSummary.abstractStage; job.stage/JobStage itself is untouched, so controlSurfacePage.ts's STAGE_LABELS/STAGE_ORDER (keyed directly on JobStage) are unaffected. state.ts now has its first real importer. Two findings surfaced: three JobStage values (experience/asset/design) are never written by any live stage.ts case (reserved, not dead, mapped to 'plan'); state.ts's 'aborted' has no JobStage equivalent at all -- unrecoverable failures currently throw rather than persisting a terminal stage. Remaining, split into WQ-023 (queued, P3): wiring the abstract vocabulary into controlSurfacePage.ts's rendered labels and build-workflow-json.ts's generated n8n workflow -- deliberately not done in WQ-019 because a mistake there risks breaking a live control surface or n8n contract this session has no way to verify against.

gaps.title: RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — diverge's K=3 candidate battle now builds in parallel through runPool/SerializedWriter
gaps.detail: The real blocker was deeper than the recordCandidate index race alone: reconceptBuild and recordCandidate both read/write a SHARED outputDir, so naive parallelization would have interleaved concurrent builds' writes to the same 5b-design.json/site/. Fixed with a shadow-directory isolation pattern (each direction builds into a symlinked copy of outputDir; only the cheap candidate-id-assignment + index-append is serialized) plus a new sourceDir option on recordCandidate. Also fixed a real ordering bug the change surfaced: runPool's results array is completion order, not task order (its docstring was wrong and is now corrected) — stage.ts now matches results back to directions by id. New regression tests prove the race is real without serialization and gone with it. Verified natively on Windows (including fs.symlink) and in the cloud sandbox: 1439/1439 native, 0 regressions.
gaps.recommendedNextStep: None — closed. See docs/MASTER_INVENTORY.json's A3 entry and commit 019367f for full detail.

gaps.title: lib/forge/battle.ts (multi-candidate Design Battle) is fully implemented and wired into the production entrypoint (opt-in) -- RESOLVED
gaps.detail: orchestrator.ts / main.ts's default single-build path is unchanged. runJob.ts's build hook can now opt into battle mode via cfg.forgeBattleMode (FORGE_BATTLE_MODE), default off. test/forge/battle.test.ts and test/workflow/forgeBattleBuild.test.ts exercise it (Playwright-dependent, sandbox-only failures, verified natively).
gaps.recommendedNextStep: RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (docs/WORK_QUEUE.json WQ-018, following WQ-007's decision): all three prerequisites WQ-007 identified are now closed. (1) Each battle candidate gets its own per-candidate repair loop in battle.ts, mirroring orchestrator.ts step 9 exactly (same exit condition, same repairCode call, same re-audit/re-capture/re-critique sequence) -- no longer a single unrepaired pass. (2) Battle spend is bounded the same way a single build's spend already is: all candidates share one routing.capabilities orchestrator instance, so remainingCents() shrinks with every candidate's real spend rather than each candidate getting a fresh budget allocation; cfg.forgeBattleCandidateCount (FORGE_BATTLE_CANDIDATES, minimum 2) additionally caps how many candidates a battle can even attempt. (3) JobState.forgeBattle is a new, dedicated field (jobState.ts), with its own summarizeForgeBattle projection (summary.ts) surfaced as JobSummary.forgeBattle -- never conflated with the classic diverge battle's designDirections/distinctnessScore/BattleSummary. runJob.ts's default build hook opts into battle mode via cfg.forgeBattleMode, default off; when on, the winner's site is copied into the run's canonical site/ directory and an all-weak/winnerless battle leaves the template build unreplaced rather than failing the run.

machine_contract.faza8_finding: The resolveCapability("...")-style seam the task asks FAZA 8 to define ALREADY EXISTS in production, fully built, for the Forge pipeline: lib/capability/orchestrator.ts's createCapabilityOrchestrator().plan(capabilityId, overrides) — literally documented in the module's own header comment as 'const plan = orchestrator.plan("craft_judging", { excludeProviders: ["gemini"] })'. This IS the machine contract.
machine_contract.closedVocabulary: CapabilityId — a closed union of 37 string literals (lib/capability/types.ts's CAPABILITY_IDS), covering exactly the categories the task named: reasoning/structured_generation/prose_writing/creative_direction/enum_direction/adversarial_critique (language); evidence_collection/evidence_research/market_research/evidence_extraction/pii_detection (evidence); vision_description/craft_judging/distinctness_judging/visual_defect_detection/image_nondepictive/image_editing/vector_generation/motion_media/audio_speech/three_d_generation (vision and media); semantic_index/design_memory (semantic); qa_measurement/visual_regression/accessibility/performance/output_security/structured_data_validation (measurement); runtime_tier/build_artifact/hosting/discoverability/observability/cost_ledger/rate_governor/human_approval (delivery and operations).
machine_contract.returnShape: CapabilityPlan { capability, descriptor, chain: PlanStep[] (ordered, executable), excluded: Exclusion[] (every dropped candidate + typed reason), plannable: boolean, estimatedCents, hasTerminal }
alreadySatisfies: 'another executor if rate/context/token/cost limits hit' -> the ranking already orders by free-then-cost-then-availability-then-latency, and execute.ts's executeCapability walks the chain on failure

'a reviewer if the result must be verified' -> isJudgement() capabilities (craft_judging, distinctness_judging, adversarial_critique, etc.) already route through the same seam as a distinct capability id, callable after the primary result
'a repair agent if QA fails' -> Hermes's decide() + the gate chain (registryGate/verdict/decide.ts) already implement escalate/continue/deliver on top of this seam
machine_contract.notYetConnected: The classic pipeline (scripts/n8n/stage.ts, the CANONICAL path per ADR 0008) still calls lib/ai/router.ts's routeCapability, not orchestrator.plan. Per the task's own FAZA 8 instruction ('do not connect the router yet if that would require large architectural changes'), this registry does NOT wire orchestrator.plan into the classic pipeline this session — that would be exactly the kind of large architectural change the MASTER RULE prohibits without dedicated justification. It is documented here as the correct FUTURE seam.
machine_contract.recommendation: Any future code that wants to write resolveCapability("image-generation") etc. should be a thin, explicitly-named wrapper over lib/capability/orchestrator.ts's existing plan()/execute() pair — NOT a third parallel implementation. This is the single most important instruction this registry can leave for the next agent (human or AI) that touches capability routing.
